projects.title_en: Synthesis of Bio-based and Biodegradable polymers from monomers from renewable Biowastes via Biocatalysis and Green Chemistry to contribute to European Circular Bioeconomy
projects.objective: Polymers-5B creates new bio-based and biodegradable polymers (polyesters, polyamides, polyphenols, polyfurans) from monomers derived from second-generation feedstocks such as tomato and olive residues, wood pulp and lignin. Using biocatalysis, green chemistry and machine-learning process optimisation under safe-and-sustainable-by-design principles, it aims for alternatives to fossil materials like PET and polyurethanes for textiles, automotive, furniture and resins.
projects.topics: bio-based polymers, biodegradable, biocatalysis, green chemistry, biowaste feedstock, safe and sustainable by design, textile fibres

projects.funding_scheme: Horizon Europe (Cluster 4, HORIZON-CL4-INDUSTRY-2025-01-MATERIALS-31, Innovation Action, Textiles for the Future Partnership)
projects.objective: ALADIN wants to show that producing clothing locally, for local markets, can be made to pay by linking existing small factories into an on-demand microfactory network run through a shared digital platform covering design, customisation, production orchestration and Digital Product Passport services. It tests the model on three demonstrator garments (a semi-automated T-shirt, a smart children's parka and a circular blazer-dress) and funds around 20 third-party SME and validation projects through open calls.

projects.title_en: Next generation automated sorting, tracing and closed-loop recycling technologies for non-rewearable textiles
projects.objective: AUTOLOOP develops technologies for textiles that can no longer be worn: AI-assisted automated sorting, chemical recycling routes and tracer additives to follow materials through the loop, moving them from lab concepts towards TRL 5. A textile data hub logs information from each recycling step in a format compatible with the Digital Product Passport, with modelling suggesting most post-consumer input could be reused or recycled.

projects.funding_scheme: Circular Bio-based Europe Joint Undertaking (CBE JU) under Horizon Europe (HORIZON-JU-CBE-2022-R-05, RIA)
projects.objective: Bio-LUSH turns under-used, non-food biomass such as hemp hurd, forestry residues, nettle and seagrass into nanocellulose fibres for functional bio-based materials. Work spans biomass refining and nano-fibrillation, breeding crops for fibre yield, a quality index for nanocellulose and machine-learning-assisted material design, with demonstrators including antibacterial textiles, edible packaging and 3D-printing filaments at TRL 5.
projects.topics: nanocellulose, biorefinery, hemp, nettle, seagrass, bio-based fibres, machine learning, antibacterial textiles

projects.title_en: Circular biobased technical textiles with innovative bio-inspired non-toxic functionalisation
projects.objective: BioFibreLoop develops recyclable technical textiles based on renewable lignin, cellulose and PLA for outdoor, sports and workwear, aiming for TRL 7. Performance such as water and oil repellence, self-cleaning and antibacterial behaviour is achieved with nature-inspired, low-waste finishing that avoids hazardous chemicals, and the technologies are demonstrated at industrial sites in Italy, Germany and Austria.
projects.topics: bio-based fibres, lignin, cellulose, PLA, biomimetic functionalisation, PFAS-free, technical textiles, outdoor and workwear

projects.objective: BioSusTex works on making cotton and cellulosic textiles easier to recycle and free of harmful substances. It covers recycling of dope-dyed man-made cellulose fibres, cleaning blended post-consumer textiles of elastane, dyes and impurities, a bio-based PFAS-free water-repellent finish and PVC-free removable prints, backed by toxicity prediction tools and a Safe-and-Sustainable-by-Design decision-support software and database.

projects.objective: CEMTex is an interregional policy-learning project on moving hospitals away from disposable medical textiles, which rely on distant supply chains and create large waste streams, towards washable and reusable alternatives. Partner regions examine obstacles in public procurement, logistics and compliance and exchange good practices to improve regional policy instruments and strengthen local circular medical-textile value chains.

projects.objective: CIRCONOMY builds a harmonised set of micro-level circular economy indicators for those poorly served by national statistics: municipalities, companies and households. It combines life-cycle and footprint methods with social science and digital tools into a modular monitoring framework and an easy-to-use app, tested in pilots and replications in Italy, Greece, Germany, the Netherlands and Lithuania and aligned with EU policy such as CSRD and the Taxonomy.

projects.title_en: Fostering circularity in textiles through interoperable solutions and best practices for implementing and harmonising EPR schemes
projects.objective: Circula-TEX supports the roll-out of extended producer responsibility (EPR) for textiles by analysing gaps in the sector and how well existing EPR schemes perform, working through stakeholder co-creation and case studies. It develops measures such as design for reuse and recycling, material identification and traceability, and a labelling system aligned with the Digital Product Passport and ESPR, ending in evidence-based criteria for harmonising EPR across Member States.

It runs pilot clusters in Denmark, Spain, Finland and Romania and an open platform where small firms can share climate-impact data, with replication planned through networks such as EIT Culture & Creativity.
